attacked_claim.quoted_headline: All 4 catalog EEW constants fall inside the structure-derived epoxy-oligomer admissibility band ... fail-closed mutation tests confirm gross-error detection.

checkA_band_width_comparison.true_manufacturer_tds_source: Hexion HCD-4022 (as transcribed in facts.json's own single_source_waiver note for resin.solid_cut_1001x75.eew_on_nv); independent of run_crosscheck.py's invented n-window.

checkB_catalog_value_status.note: The catalog value itself (500.0) is a safe midpoint of the true TDS band and so passes under either band; this check targets the BAND's own claimed provenance and detection power, not this single value.

checkD_mutation_replay_against_cc_v1_own.method: Each probe value is tested with constant-crosscheck-v1's OWN admissibility predicate (eew_to_n + 1.5<=n<=3.5), replayed verbatim from run_crosscheck.py.

closes: Demonstrates that constant-crosscheck-v1's solid-resin EEW admissibility band is looser than the manufacturer TDS band already recorded in-repo for the identical fact, and that this gap is not merely theoretical: constant-crosscheck-v1's own predicate fails to flag realistic wrong-grade EEW values inside the gap.
does_not_close: Does not show the catalog VALUE (500.0) is wrong -- it is well inside both bands.
Does not affect the liquid-DGEBA sub-check (3/4 constants), whose n in [0,0.2] band is tight and literature-anchored.
Does not modify facts.json, the module manifest, or any locked dataset.

Gap probe values are illustrative EEW numbers, not verified transcriptions of a real competing product's TDS; they demonstrate the admissibility predicate's detection power, not an actual catalog error.
headline: constant-crosscheck-v1's solid-resin EEW admissibility band [[383.5, 667.8]] is 2.84x wider than the manufacturer TDS band [[450.0, 550.0]] already cited in-repo for the identical fact (resin.solid_cut_1001x75.eew_on_nv); 4/4 realistic gap-zone probe values are admitted by constant-crosscheck-v1's own predicate without being flagged, refuting its fail-closed gross-error-detection claim for the solid-resin EEW sub-check.
hypothesis: constant-crosscheck-v1's solid_type1_epoxy admissibility band ([1.5<=n<=3.5], EEW [383.5,667.8]) is claimed structure-derived and fail-closed. If the manufacturer-published TDS band already cited in-repo for this exact fact (Hexion HCD-4022, 450-550 g/eq NV) is strictly narrower, and physically-real EEW values exist that fall inside constant-crosscheck-v1's band but outside the true TDS band without being flagged, the fail-closed gross-error-detection claim is refuted for this constant family.

inputs.fact_note_raw: Hexion HCD-4022 direct read (450-550 on nonvolatiles)

non_circularity: The true manufacturer TDS band used for comparison is read from facts.json's own single_source_waiver note field (populated at catalog-authoring time from the Hexion HCD-4022 TDS), which is a different provenance channel than run_crosscheck.py's hardcoded [1.5,3.5] n-window (invented at audit-authoring time); comparing the two is a genuine in-repo cross-check, not a self-referential re-read of the audit script's own constants.
purpose: Falsification attack on constant-crosscheck-v1 Check-1's claim that the solid-epoxy EEW admissibility band is structure-derived and that its fail-closed mutation tests confirm gross-error detection, by comparing constant-crosscheck-v1's self-computed band against the manufacturer TDS band already recorded in facts.json's own single_source_waiver note for the identical fact.

theory_reference.eew_oligomer_series: Ellis 1993 (ISBN 978-0-7514-0095-6); Lee & Neville 1967, Handbook of Epoxy Resins -- cited by constant-crosscheck-v1 as the basis for its band, but does not tabulate the [1.5,3.5] n-window used for the solid-resin class.
theory_reference.manufacturer_tds_band: Hexion HCD-4022 EPON Resin 1001-X-75, EEW 450-550 g/eq on nonvolatiles (as transcribed into facts.json's single_source_waiver note at catalog-authoring time).

verdict.explanation: constant-crosscheck-v1's solid_type1_epoxy admissibility band is 284.3 g/eq wide (2.84x wider than the 100 g/eq manufacturer TDS band already cited in-repo for the same fact). 4 of 4 physically-real probe EEW values fall inside constant-crosscheck-v1's own admissible band, outside the true manufacturer band, and are NOT flagged by constant-crosscheck-v1's own predicate -- directly contradicting its headline claim that 'fail-closed mutation tests confirm gross-error detection' for this constant family. The band's [1.5,3.5] n-window is not sourced from the cited literature (Ellis 1993 / Lee & Neville 1967 tabulate no such range); it is wider than the manufacturer spec its own inline comment cites as justification.
